text: After a long journey, you finally arrive at the academy. A clerk directs you to the administration office. The administrator asks you for tuition fees.

We'll learn magic crafting by making cards. Today you'll start by familiarizing yourself with the different card types.

Green is the color of nature, growth, health and savagery.

Black is the color of industry, machines, organization and decay.

Red is the color of chaos, aggression, freedom and speed.

Blue is the color of subterfuge, control, magic and knowledge.

Get a deck, noob!

This is an enchanting class. Here, you'll learn how to modify existing cards. For now, let's start with Augmentation: it makes a card more powerful in exchange for higher mana requirements. Here is some magic dust, it's an essential component for any magic crafting.
Moly tells you she appreciated the way you made her feel welcome. She offers you a token of gratitude, pick your favorite!

Molly finds you with an armful of notes and a shy, hopeful smile. She says she has been wanting to study together, and that she would love to share a few tricks from the green magic she knows best—if you can spare an evening at the library soon.

Molly finds you again with a shy brightness that was not there before. She says your friendship has come to mean more to her than she quite knows how to say, and she wants you to have something from her own collection—a card she has kept close. She lays a few favorites before you and asks you to choose the one that speaks to you.

Molly finds you with a hopeful bounce in her step and asks if you would like to go hiking in the Gray Mountains. She talks about the trail, the overlook, and the clear air on a bright weekend, and waits to see whether you will come along.

parameters.text: Molly's smile falters. She nods quickly, trying to hide her disappointment, and says maybe another time.

text: Before long you are both on a bright weekend trail in the Gray Mountains, wind in the pines. Molly sets an easy, tireless pace while your lungs burn and your legs complain, but she never leaves you behind—slowing on the steep bits, offering a hand over the rocks, and laughing with you when you stop to catch your breath. By the overlook you are worn out and grinning, glad you said yes.

Molly seeks you out with a thoughtful look. She says she has been watching how you carry yourself, and she respects the care you put into your work. She asks if you would take on a mentoring post with her at the library on Tuesday evenings, helping younger students find their footing.

job.name: Library Mentoring
job.description: Help younger students at the library under Molly's guidance.

text: Molly seeks you out again, this time with a small pouch clutched in her hands. She says she has grown to respect how you work beside her, and she wants you to have something she makes herself—a strand of beads she has been stringing for you. She offers them freely, though she glances toward her dust pouch as if she would understand if you preferred something more ordinary.

Molly finds you with a tight smile that does not reach her eyes. Whatever has soured between you still sits heavy on her, and she makes no effort to hide it. She presses a small purse into your hands anyway, calling it charity for someone who clearly needs the help, and waits to see whether you will take the slight.

Molly draws you aside, cheeks flushed, and admits she has noticed the way you have been flirting with her. She does not sound angry so much as uncertain, and she asks you plainly what your intentions are—whether this is a game, or something you mean to pursue.

parameters.text: Molly's face falls. She nods a little too quickly and looks away, clearly a bit upset, before murmuring that she must have misunderstood.

text: Molly finds you with a soft, eager smile and asks if you would go out with her again—this time to the Royal Pigeon Inn. She has already thought it through: she knows coin is tight for you, so she is inviting you as her guest, and she hopes you will say yes.

Molly leans in close, voice low, and asks if you would come with her to her room at the Royal Pigeon Inn. There is no mistaking the invitation—she wants you alone with her, and she is waiting on your answer.

Molly catches your sleeve in the morning bustle and pulls you aside, a little breathless. She promised the kitchen staff she would lend a hand today, but the prep work has piled higher than she expected and she still has lessons waiting. She looks at you hopefully and asks if you would help her in the kitchens.

parameters.text: You and Molly spend the morning in the kitchens, flour on your sleeves and laughter over simmering pots. The work goes faster with two, and by the time the trays are ready you are both grinning and a little sticky.
Molly's face falls. She nods quickly, trying to hide her disappointment, and hurries off toward the kitchens alone.

text: Still warm from the kitchens, Molly tells you she really enjoyed cooking with you. With a shy, hopeful smile she proposes a pajamas night at her place—good books, hot chocolate, and nowhere else to be.

parameters.text: Molly's eyes light up. She already looks forward to pajamas, books, and hot chocolate with you.
Molly's smile falters. She nods quickly, trying to hide her disappointment, and says maybe another time.

text: Evening finds you at Molly's place in pajamas, a mug of hot chocolate warming your hands and a stack of good books between you. Hours slip by in soft talk and shared pages until the hour grows late. At the door, as you prepare to leave, Molly looks up at you, waiting to see how you will say good night.

parameters.text: You lean in and kiss Molly good evening. She softens into it, cheeks warm, and murmurs a shy good night as you step into the hall.
You cheerfully thank Molly for the books, the chocolate, and the company. She beams, clearly pleased, and waves you off with a bright good night.

text: You come upon Elsa angrily reprimanding Molly in the morning hall. Elsa insists it is not befitting Molly's rank to meddle with servants, her voice sharp with wounded pride. It seems Molly tried to help the serving staff with their work, and Elsa, a proud noble, took the gesture as an affront to the order she holds dear.

parameters.text: Molly's eyes fill with tears as she shrinks back from Elsa's rebuke. Elsa softens once she sees you take her side, her anger ebbing into a stiff, satisfied calm.
Molly draws a shaky breath, then finds her courage and stands up to Elsa. Her voice is quiet but firm as she defends helping those who need it, and Elsa falls briefly silent.

text: As you greet Molly, she takes you by the hand and insists there is something you really need to do. Surprised, you follow her to a gym room lined with weights and mats. She nods toward a rack, encourages you to lift, and winks as if daring you to show her what you can do.

parameters.text: Molly stares as you hoist the weight with ease, clearly surprised by your strength.
The bar barely budges, but Molly only grins and urges you on, cheering every shaky attempt.
Molly flushes with pleasure at the compliment, clearly flattered, and demonstrates another clean lift with a shy smile.

text: Emma catches your eyes drifting from the page and asks, with a knowing smile, whether you are having trouble focusing. Her legs are crossed just so beneath the shorts she somehow always wears on the evenings you study together—and no, she assures you, that is not a coincidence. She lets the tease hang a moment, then cools into a sharper truth: charm alone will not win her. For now you do not stand a chance; her respect comes first.

You notice Emma nearby and gather the courage to go speak to her, only to find yourself stunned by her charm—every word you meant to say slips away the moment her eyes meet yours. She watches your struggle with clear amusement, then teases you gently about the tongue-tied display before turning away with a smile that stays with you after she is gone.

Emma is amused by your persistence in trying to woo her. She pretends to send you away with a cool little wave, then calls you back before you have gone three steps—she has an idea for how you might make yourself useful. She is attending a ball at the Academy and needs a faire valoir at her side. Wear your best, she says, and do not dare be late.

parameters.text: Emma's amusement fades. She had offered you a place at her side, and your refusal leaves her clearly disappointed.

text: Emma greets you at the Academy ball with a bright, practiced smile, already weighing every glance from the professors and patrons she means to impress. She draws you close and makes it plain she is counting on you tonight—how you carry yourself beside her is part of the figure she wants to cut. The music swells, the room watches, and she waits to see which face you will show at her side.

parameters.text: Emma softens with quiet appreciation; your restraint has helped her more than flash ever would.
Emma's smile thins. She had counted on you, and the evening leaves her disappointed.
Emma looks genuinely surprised, then impressed—she had not expected you to shine quite like that.
Emma's smile thins. She had counted on you, and the evening leaves her disappointed.

text: Emma sizes you up with a cool, appraising glance, as if grading a paper she already knows will need work. She decides quickly that your academic footing could use a firmer hand—hers—and offers to host private study sessions in her rooms, for a fee she names without apology.

parameters.text: Emma's expression cools. She had offered you her time and expertise, and your refusal leaves her plainly disappointed.

text: Emma is plainly vexed at having lost to you, though she keeps her chin high and offers a crisp, dignified congratulations. She allows herself one dry joke about beginner's luck—then waits, as if daring you to take the victory as anything less than temporary.

parameters.text: You congratulate her in turn, saying you are glad to have found a worthy opponent. Emma's shoulders ease a fraction; the sting of the loss softens into something closer to respect.
You taunt her over the loss. Emma's composure cracks—her eyes flash, and she answers with a sharp, angry edge that promises she will not forget.

text: Emma's usual sharp composure has slipped; worry sits plainly on her face, and when you ask what is wrong she hesitates before answering. She confides that her student loan has become a problem—her parents are poor and cannot help her through it. Studying is her whole life, and the thought that she might have to leave the Academy has her voice tight with fear.

parameters.text: Together you dig through the contract and find a way to restructure the terms. Emma is visibly relieved, and her thanks are warm and genuine.
You pore over the clauses together, but nothing useful surfaces. Emma's disappointment is quiet, but plain.
Emma accepts the gold with a careful nod, clearly thankful for the help when she needs it most.
You shrug and leave her to it. Emma frowns after you, the worry on her face hardening into something colder.

text: Emma is cracking jokes in the middle of a knot of students, every punchline landing while all eyes stay fixed on her. You edge closer through the laughter and find yourself weighing how to join in—whether to ride the wave with the others, or risk a quip of your own.

parameters.text: Emma lights up when she sees you laughing with the others, plainly glad her jokes land with you too.
Emma lights up when she sees you laughing with the others, plainly glad her jokes land with you too.
You slip in a joke of your own. Emma throws her head back laughing, clearly impressed you kept pace with her.
You try a joke of your own—and it flops. The circle goes quiet for a beat before Emma steers the banter elsewhere.

text: Emma draws you aside with a cool, purposeful look—she has heard of a rare mushroom that grows only in the Forest of Schlupak, and she is convinced it will sharpen her conjuration work considerably. The woods are dangerous, she admits without softening it, which is why she wants company. She proposes you join her next weekend, share the risk, and split whatever you find.

You and Emma push deeper into the Forest of Schlupak, gathering ingredients among the roots and damp shade. She crouches to pluck a cluster of rare magical mushrooms—then a dark bear crests a small hill above you, shoulders rolling, eyes fixed, and the woods go suddenly quiet.

parameters.text: You draw a sword and drive the bear off. Emma stares after it, unable to believe her eyes.
Emma bails you out with a clever magical device that distracts the bear long enough for you both to flee.
You run to draw the bear away, then feign death until it loses interest and lumbers off. Emma is plainly impressed.
Emma bails you out with a clever magical device that distracts the bear long enough for you both to flee.

text: Henry finds you with urgent news—Emma has fallen ill and is resting in the hospital wing. You rush to her bedside and find her lying there, pale but smiling. A little embarrassed, she admits she tried a new concoction on herself because she did not have time to fetch a test bot—even she can make mistakes, she says, though she hopes to be out by tomorrow.

parameters.text: You return with a small bouquet. Emma's smile widens as she takes it in, clearly cheered by the gesture.
Emma softens at the worry in your voice; she looks touched that you care so openly.
Your concern comes out clumsy and overdone. Emma laughs it off kindly, but the moment slips past.

text: Emma watches your latest attempt with a look half amused and half heartwarmed, as if she has been waiting for you to try again. She shakes her head, then softens. "Alright, alright, Fibonacci... I think you've earned a date." Her eyes brighten as she asks where the two of you should go.

Emma catches the eager look in your eyes and laughs, clearly enjoying how keen you are for a second date. She tilts her head, teasing, then offers something better: come to her room for a very special experience—one she promises you will not forget.

parameters.text: There is simply no polite—or impolite—way to refuse an invitation like that. You accept before your better judgment can clear its throat.

text: You show up at Emma's door buzzing with hope for a romantic evening—only to find her in a crafting outfit, sleeves rolled and tools already laid out. "Ah, here you are," she says brightly. "Take the tools and help me." The hours slip by as you craft a card together at her workbench. It is not the night you imagined, but you are happy simply to be with her. When she presses the finished card into your hands and winks at the illustration, you smile, hopeful for what comes next.

Emma looks you over with a smile that is half invitation and half verdict, then takes you apart with a few sharp, amused remarks until you have nowhere left to hide. When she is finished, her tone softens into something more deliberate: you have earned a real shot at her, she says—but she will not give herself to anyone less than the best. Win the league, and she will be yours.

parameters.text: Emma's eyes brighten with genuine appreciation. She likes that you did not flinch.
Emma laughs, then leans in and kisses you lightly on the cheek—a tease, and a promise she will not quite make yet.

text: Emma approaches you looking more vulnerable than usual—nearly shy, as if the wager she set has finally caught up with her. She reminds you of her promise: win the league, and she would be yours. Now that you have the title, she proposes you come to her room to collect your winnings.

Emma approaches you with unusual hesitation, as if the words she needs cost her something. She admits—reluctantly, and with carefully measured pride—that she has come to respect your skill, and that a reliable teammate would serve her ascent in society, starting with winning more tournaments. She asks whether you would join her, proposing Thursday evenings to train together.

parameters.text: Emma's composure holds, but disappointment flickers plainly across her face. She had offered you a place at her side, and your refusal leaves her cool and quiet.

text: Elsa finds you with Ousmane, Henry, and Molly, giggling with barely contained excitement as she urges you all to follow—there is something hilarious she needs you to see. She leads you to a quiet room where Emma is alone at the barre, holding a long, poised leg stretch with perfect form. Elsa stifles a mocking laugh at the sight; Molly murmurs that it looks cool, while Ousmane and Henry go silent, staring. Elsa bristles at their reaction and Molly chuckles under her breath—until Emma notices the audience, stops mid-hold, and raises an eyebrow. Everyone scatters but you.

parameters.text: You blush and compliment her form before bolting after the others. Emma's eyebrow softens; she relaxes and smiles.
Emma is impressed and says you would make a good dance partner.
Emma laughs gently and helps you through the steps.

text: This is an artificery class. Here, we'll learn how to create new cards. Conjuration consists in creating a new card from scratch. Try it!

Before enchanting class, the academy sometimes runs a sports hour—mostly laps, and plenty of them. Across the track you spot Emma and Molly jogging side by side, chatting pleasantly as they go. Molly looks thoroughly at ease, sporty and unfazed, while Emma is clearly struggling to keep up, gasping between words as she tries to hold the conversation.

parameters.text: You compliment Molly on her shape. She beams, clearly pleased.
You compliment Emma on her figure. She scoffs—but you catch her smile.
You taunt Emma as you pass them. She smirks.

text: At the cafeteria, Emma and Elsa sit over coffee in a thinly veiled contest of wit and poise, each clearly intent on outshining the other. You take a seat and try to ease the tension with a deliberately stupid joke. Emma laughs, amused despite herself, while Elsa looks distinctly annoyed.

parameters.text: Your second joke lands flat. Emma offers a polite smile; Elsa does not bother.
